Subject: Tenant provisioning & egress validation for ACME private deployment

Hi Hannah / Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — ACME liked the idea of a private deployment with tenant-level isolation. Before we spin up the dedicated VPC we need to validate a few networking and egress items so NetOps can sign the provisioning ticket.

High-level asks from our side:
- Confirm the outbound egress endpoints that the control plane will need to reach (we run strict allowlists)
- Any requirement for static egress IPs or will dynamic NAT be acceptable?
- Expected proxy/TLS termination behaviour for customer-facing data plane egress
- Tenant provisioning SLA and expected time-to-provision once ACME gives the green light

I've attached our procurement contact and proposed maintenance windows in the Doc we shared; Carlos is CC'd on the NetOps side and will handle the allowlist once we have definitive endpoints.

Can you confirm the list of control-plane/public endpoints and whether you can provide a CSV we can drop straight into our firewall system?

Thanks,
Sabrina

Sabrina Lowe
Sr. Cloud Architect, ACME Cloud
Sabrina.Lowe@acme.com

Subject: Re: Tenant provisioning & egress validation for ACME private deployment

Thanks Sabrina — good list. Attaching a concise playbook (redwood-tenant-provisioning-playbook-v1.pdf) and a starter CSV that contains the control-plane hostnames and recommended ports.

Quick answers up-front:
- Control plane outbound: HTTPS to our control endpoints (cntrl-1.redwood.net, cntrl-2.redwood.net), plus TLS to telemetry.redwood.net:443 for traces/metrics.
- Static egress IP: we can offer a small set of static NAT egress IPs for Dedicated/Private customers (recommended for strict allowlists). If ACME prefers dynamic NAT, we'll need to extend the TTL on our routing updates — that adds a small operational window but is supported.
- Proxy/TLS termination: data plane egress from inference nodes must preserve end-to-end TLS; we support both TLS passthrough and mTLS to customer endpoints. If ACME's proxy terminates TLS, we'll need to configure mutual auth between the proxy and the egress gateway.
- SLA & provisioning: once we have signed SOW and allowlist confirmed, standard tenant build time for a Private deployment is 5 business days (includes networking changes + cert provisioning). We can compress to 2–3 days for P1 customers if required.

Action items for ACME:
1) Confirm if you require static egress IPs (see column B in the CSV).
2) Provide the firewall team contact and preferred maintenance windows.
3) Review the attached playbook and mark any items you want redlined for your internal compliance.

I'll loop Jonas and Irene here for the network diagram and specific NAT/IP allocations.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

On Mon, Nov 1, 2026 at 10:03 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick answers up-front:
> - Control plane outbound: HTTPS to our control endpoints (cntrl-1.redwood.net, cntrl-2.redwood.net), plus TLS to telemetry.redwood.net:443 for traces/metrics.

Fwding a short network diagram and a minimal ops checklist (network-diagrams-acme-vpc-v2.png). Notes from the networking side:
- Preferred pattern: control-plane components initiate outbound TLS to Redwood-managed endpoints on port 443. No inbound ports to ACME required for control plane.
- If you require static egress IPs, we will allocate up to 4 addresses per tenancy to be advertised via NAT gateway. These are reachable from ACME's allowlist and will be stable across minor maintenance windows.
- Egress for large-scale model downloads: we recommend using a signed S3 presigned URL pattern with a short-lived token; this avoids adding long-lived IPs to your allowlist.
- On proxy: if ACME terminates TLS at your perimeter proxy, we suggest configuring an inner mTLS channel to the egress gateway. We can supply certs and rotation schedules (Irene will own the rotation notes).

Operational checklist (short):
1) Confirm static vs dynamic NAT (deadline: 2026-11-05)
2) Approve maintenance window (we propose Sun 11/14 00:00–04:00 UTC)
3) Provide firewall CIDR control point (CSV accepted)
4) Sign off on the playbook redlines (Hannah will track)

I've attached the diagram and included example CIDRs in the CSV. Let us know if you'd like a short call to walk NetOps through the allowlist import.

- Jonas

- TLS behaviour: ACME will continue TLS termination at our edge proxy; we want mTLS between the proxy and Redwood egress gateway. Please provide cert details and rotation cadence.
